top_story.headline: Rep. Dan Crenshaw still has no 2025 annual financial disclosure on file, 72 days past his final extension
top_story.dek: He is the only sitting member flagged by this morning's Deadline Watch check.
paragraphs: Rep. Dan Crenshaw (R-TX-2) filed for an extension on 6/4/2026. The final extended deadline was 8/13/2026, and the Clerk of the House index shows no calendar year 2025 annual report from him as of today, 72 days later.

The check compares every sitting member against the Clerk of the House index and Senate eFD. A filing under an unexpected spelling of a name can read as missing, so the result is unconfirmed. The Senate half of the check failed today (see the footer), so it covers House members only.

The other deadline item is that seven Senate-confirmed officials have no posted certification of ethics-agreement compliance, 220 to 417 days past due. The longest overdue is Michelle White Bowman, Governor and Vice Chairman for Supervision of the Federal Reserve System Board of Governors, confirmed 6/4/2025 with certification due 9/2/2025.

sections.eyebrow: Contacts With the President, VP & Cabinet
sections.headline: No logged FARA contacts today; one lobbying report names the President and Vice President
paragraphs: No FARA filings in the Top Officials scan were new, so there are no foreign-agent contacts with the President, Vice President or cabinet officials to report. One LDA filing lists the President and Vice President among the entities lobbied.

items: Military Officers Association of America (self-filing, 3rd Quarter report): entities lobbied include the Office of the Vice President, the President and the Vice President. Issues listed include the Love Lives On Act of 2025 (H.R. 1004), the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act (H.R. 3838), TRICARE Select enrollment for pregnancy (H.R. 4381), the Health Care Fairness for Military Families Act of 2025 (H.R. 4768), and veteran and spouse licensing (H.R. 5035). LDA filing.

sections.headline: Three federal officials filed terminations; director-level appointees report securities transactions and ethics certifications
paragraphs: Three federal officials—including two U.S. Marshals—filed termination or resignation notifications with OGE this week. Meanwhile, multiple cabinet-level and sub-cabinet officials reported periodic securities transactions and annual ethics agreement compliance certifications, reflecting routine divestiture and portfolio management activity among newly appointed senior staff.

sections.headline: No new House or Senate disclosures in this morning's input
paragraphs: The input has no unreported House filings and no Senate filings from 2026-10-21 onward. sections.headline: 10 new registrations and 5 terminations, led by drone-defense, tariff and biofuel clients

blocks.text: Tracking 483 Senate-confirmed officials with ethics agreements since Jan. 20, 2025. Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.
